Hi Tom — quick technical note from infra:

Calendly will display the timeslot in the viewer’s browser timezone, but the ICS file is generated with the organizer’s timezone metadata. If the organizer account is set to America/New_York and the viewer is in Europe/London around DST transitions, importing the ICS into some calendar clients will shift by one hour.

Workarounds we use:
- Force tz in scheduling links (Chili Piper supports an explicit tz query param). Example fallback: https://app.chilipiper.com/meet/laura?tz=Europe%2FLondon (paste this directly).
- Generate and attach an ICS converted to the attendee timezone (I’ve created dylan_eu_converted.ics and attached it).
- Ask attendees to confirm the timezone dropdown in Calendly before booking — it’s subtle but there’s a selector at the top right of the Calendly booking page.

If Tom confirms Tue 09:00 GMT I’ll publish the converted ICS and we’ll use the Chili Piper link for any future bookings to avoid the edge case.

—Dylan
